summary.headline: Apar Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 29.1% to INR6,591 crore and PAT rose 77.7% to INR467 crore, a record quarter.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 29.1% YoY to INR6,591 crore, with EBITDA post open-period forex up 62.7% to INR814 crore and margin at 12.4% versus 9.8%. PAT rose 77.7% to INR467 crore (7.1% margin), which management called the highest quarterly sales and profit in company history. Oil division was the largest incremental contributor, helped by inventory gains on rising fuel prices, partly offset by a ~INR94 crore provision. Conductor volumes fell 6.7% as customers deferred manufacturing clearance on conventional conductors amid the aluminium price spike, while premium mix rose. Management declined to answer guidance, forecast or funding questions because of a pending shareholder approval for securities issuance.

segments.name: Conductors
segments.commentary: Revenue INR3,338 crore (+19.9%) on volume down 6.7%; domestic revenue +19.3%, export +22.2%, export mix 20.5%. Premium products were 50.3% of revenue vs 43.7% a year ago. EBITDA INR285 crore, +14%. Pending order book ~INR10,190 crore (56.8% export); new orders INR5,245 crore (65.8% export), including over INR2,800 crore from two overseas utilities (one US, one Europe).

segments.name: Oil (specialty oils)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,701 crore (+34.7%) with volume 129,085 kL (-13.7%); India volume -4.4%, transformer oil domestic -6.2%, auto oil +6.6%, industrial lubricants +12.1%. UAE Hamriyah plant curtailed by port closure. EBITDA INR329 crore, lifted by inventory gains as crude and gas oil prices rose; ~INR94 crore provision booked for price reversal.

segments.name: Cables
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,838 crore (+29.5%); domestic +59.9%, export -13.7%, export mix 27.6%. US revenue up ~2.5% YoY. Pending order book INR1,925 crore vs INR1,653 crore a year ago. EBITDA INR194 crore, margin 10.6%.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to provide guidance, projections or forecasts, and did not address proposed funding, citing shareholder approval process for securities issuance.
Cable EBITDA margin cited as in line with the company's stated 10% to 11% range.

Most of the conductor order book (excluding two large export orders) expected to execute within about a year; a few orders may spill into the next year; the two large utility orders run over multiple years.
Management said the Q1 volume shortfall in conductors is temporary, as delayed orders have penalty clauses for delay.
Management would not say whether oil margins of this level will recur, citing price volatility.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation across divisions ranges 80% to 90% by product category.
Company is undertaking significant capex to debottleneck and build capacity; detail referenced to prior calls, no new figures given.
Received approval from a large US utility for OPGW with 144 fibre counts.
Achieved its highest-ever reconductoring installations in the quarter, including HTLS.
Inventory in specialty oils was reduced during the quarter, with more just-in-time purchasing.
demand_pricing: Conductor volume down 6.7% as customers held manufacturing clearance on conventional (e.g., AL-59) conductors after aluminium price spikes; management says premium segments continued to execute.
Oil: destocking by customers after supply normalised; management said secondary sales held up and primary sales fell.
Cables: wires sales +46%; active towns +17%, distributors +25%, retail accounts +51%; channel business +92%.
US cables: approvals obtained from three large data-centre operators; company now bidding RFQs for copper LV and MV cables, previously aluminium-only.
US conductors: about 70% of the market is served by local production; import share (~30%) is where APAR competes. Section 232 tariff on aluminium and conductors is 50%; customers are paying it.
Metal premiums (MJP) cannot be hedged; company locks premium through supplier contracts. Oil purchases are about 65% contract-based and 35% spot.

qa_highlights.question: Why was oil EBITDA about INR25,000 per kL, and will it recur?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to low-cost historical inventory being sold at higher market prices as fuel prices rose. It would not say whether such margins recur, and noted provisions were made as of 30 June per accounting standards.

qa_highlights.question: Why were US exports weak, and when will they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a Section 232 disruption in the prior quarter halted US orders, and most US deliveries are on DDP terms, so revenue recognition lagged. It said recent approvals and two large utility contracts support future shipments.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the conductor backlog is executable and what is its geographic mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding the two large orders, most backlog should execute in about a year, with some spill-over. Exports (56.8% of INR10,190 crore) are spread across North and South America, Europe, Africa, and Asia.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book is HVDC and premium products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said HVDC ordering so far is small; one US utility order includes a high-voltage line, and most HVDC ordering is still to come. No specific premium share in the book was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a difference in margin between domestic and export conductors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export margins depend on product specification and do not always run lower. Domestic conventional products earn lower margins than export ones because of quality standards. Blended EBITDA per ton was given; the split was not.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume and realisation split for cables and conductors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave revenue growth only, not volume, and said US sales by geography are not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: How are metal-price swings affecting demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said primary sales fell due to customer stocking and deferral, while secondary sales held up and fundamental demand is intact.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital position?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is 45 to 50 days, broadly stable; conductor debtor and inventory days improved QoQ.

risks_watch: Oil inventory-gain reversal: contract purchases (about 65%) lag spot prices; falling prices could reverse margins, and the ~INR94 crore provision signals this risk.
Conductor clearance deferrals: volume recovery depends on customers resuming manufacturing clearance; penalty clauses limit delay.
Metal premium (MJP) exposure is unhedgeable and is locked only through supplier contracts.
US tariffs: Section 232 at 50% on aluminium and conductors; Section 301 at about 10% for India is still under review.
Shareholder approval for securities issuance and proposed funding were not discussed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the reported numbers and execution, but guarded on forward view: management repeatedly declined guidance, forecast and funding questions under the pending securities approval process. Explanations for the oil margin and US export lag were detailed but stopped short of forecasts.
key_quotes: This incidentally is the highest quarterly sales as well as profit number that we have achieved in the history of the company.
So we've actually played absolutely by the book.
Much of India's ordering is still to come.
So it's a completely flexible game. I mean there's no single rule to it yet.

growth.why: No numeric guidance was given; management declined to answer forecast questions citing a pending securities issuance approval. Backing is a conductor order book of about INR10,190 crore plus INR1,925 crore in cables, and unquantified capex ("significant capex", no new figures), so growth outlook is only modestly positive.
